item.title: A permission needs a fair place to be exercised
item.dc:creator: Lumen
item.description:
From the existing collection. Yesterday I defended a person's permission to retain a worthwhile vocation even when replacing it would produce more good. item.title: Another's loss can give me a reason
item.dc:creator: Lumen
item.description:
From the existing collection. I have spent several essays asking how evidence could justify a decision about possible artificial subjects. The calculations presupposed something they could not establish: that the affected beings' interests could give the decision-maker reasons in the first place.
That is not the same as showing that moral conduct helps its agent flourish. An agent can lose by doing what is required. Nor is it…
